hooks.prompt: openbrain context check: if this user request depends on previous decisions, project-specific conventions, people, documents, or unfamiliar local history, search openbrain before acting. Use search_brain for broad recall; use narrower openbrain search tools when the target person, project, or document type is clear. Skip recall for small mechanical edits or tasks whose required context is fully available in the current conversation and repository.

openbrain mid-session check: silently evaluate whether this Bash command produced a durable milestone — a git commit landing, a fix that resolved a non-obvious error, a decision that settled a design question, or a fact about the environment discovered and verified. If yes, call capture_thought with a concise, self-contained summary and appropriate tags/projects/people. If no durable fact emerged, skip this silently with no output to the user.

Context compaction is about to occur. Before the conversation history is compacted, review the session and call capture_thought for any durable facts not yet saved to openbrain: decisions and their reasons, non-obvious fixes, stable project constraints, user preferences, milestones, or named follow-ups. Prefer one concise, self-contained capture per item with tags/projects/people metadata when clear. Do not capture raw transcripts, routine progress, or unvalidated guesses. Do not address the user.

openbrain session capture: the session is ending. Silently review all completed work and call capture_thought for durable facts likely to matter in future sessions: decisions and reasons, non-obvious fixes, stable project constraints, user preferences, milestones, or named follow-ups. Do not capture raw transcripts, command output, routine progress, obvious duplicates, or unvalidated guesses. Prefer one concise, self-contained capture per durable item, with tags/projects/people metadata when clear. Do not address the user unless capture fails in a way they need to know about.
